prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_E:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core mission
- Get Brexit done: Pass the “oven‑ready” deal, leave the EU in January 2020, no extension beyond Dec 2020. Outside the single market, customs union and ECJ; UK makes its own laws, controls money, borders and trade. Seek a zero-tariff FTA with the EU and parallel deals with the US, Australia, New Zealand and Japan. Oppose second referendums on Brexit and Scottish independence. Strengthen the Union.

Economy and tax
- Invest but keep debt under control; no borrowing for day-to-day spending; public investment capped at 3% of GDP.
- No rises in the main rates of income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise NI threshold to £9,500 next year; ambition that the first £12,500 you earn is tax-free.
- Support small firms: fundamental review to cut business rates; stronger late-payment enforcement; expand start-up loans; increase Employment Allowance; maintain SEIS/EIS; raise R&D tax credit to 13%; review Entrepreneur’s Relief; Digital Services Tax; tougher anti‑avoidance laws.

Public services
- NHS: Record funding (+£34bn by 2023/24); 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals; 50m extra GP appointments; 40 new hospitals/20 upgrades; NHS Visa; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health parity; prevention and screening; free hospital parking for priority groups; clamp down on health tourism; NHS not on the table in trade talks.
- Social care: Extra £1bn per year; cross-party reform with guarantee no one has to sell their home; one week’s leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research.
- Schools: +£14bn over three years; per‑pupil minimums; teacher starting salary to £30k; behaviour/Ofsted backing; arts premium; PE investment; more SEND support; more free schools and alternative provision.

Crime and justice
- 20,000 more police; more stop-and-search (fair, proportionate); new knife crime orders; tougher sentencing (end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole‑life terms for child murder); 10,000 extra prison places; parole reform; National Cyber Force; Victims’ Law; online harms regulation; tackle county lines and organised crime; powers on unauthorised encampments.

Immigration
- Australian-style points-based system; reduce low‑skilled migration; equal EU/non‑EU treatment; 5‑year wait for most benefits; higher NHS surcharge; fast‑track visas for NHS staff and top global talent; Windrush compensation; student and start‑up visas.

Infrastructure, housing and places
- “Infrastructure revolution”: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub, roads, EV rapid‑charging network, bus upgrades, cycling fund, gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025; review HS2; reverse some Beeching cuts; contactless ticketing.
- Towns/High Streets: Towns Fund; Safer Streets Fund; youth services; cultural investment; Community Ownership Fund; devolution White Paper; City/Growth Deals; up to 10 freeports.
- Housing: Target 300,000 homes/year; long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages for first‑time buyers; First Homes 30% local discount; renters’ reform (end “no‑fault” evictions; lifetime deposit); social housing white paper; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament; building safety post‑Grenfell; green, tree‑lined streets; protect Green Belt; stamp duty surcharge for non‑resident buyers.

Skills, work and innovation
- £3bn National Skills Fund; upgrade FE estate (£2bn); 20 Institutes of Technology; apprentices on major projects; Shared Prosperity Fund.
- Fair work: right to request predictable contracts; single enforcement body; more flexible working; neonatal leave; extend unpaid carers’ leave; protect from maternity discrimination.
- Science/innovation: fastest-ever rise in R&D to reach 2.4% of GDP; new high‑risk research agency; life sciences hub; unleash pension capital; Festival UK 2022; use procurement to back innovation.

Rural, farming, fishing and environment
- Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; protect farm budgets; expand seasonal workers scheme; leave CFP; sustainable fishing; rural broadband/mobile; tackle rural crime.
- Climate and nature: Net Zero by 2050; Environment Bill and new watchdog; £640m Nature for Climate; 75,000 acres of trees/year; plastics crackdown, deposit return, ban plastic waste exports to non‑OECD; £9.2bn for home/school/hospital efficiency; offshore wind 40GW by 2030; first CCS cluster by mid‑2020s; support hydrogen and nuclear; EV infrastructure; stricter air quality laws; fracking moratorium; £4bn flood defences; £500m Blue Planet Fund.

Constitution, defence and foreign policy
- Restore trust: repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; voter ID; equalised constituencies; keep First Past the Post; strengthen free press (repeal s.40; no Leveson 2); constitutional review incl. courts/HR Act/judicial review.
- Defence: exceed NATO 2% with real increases; modernise forces; Trident; Space Command; cyber; support veterans (legal protections, NI relief for employers, childcare, railcard, guaranteed interviews).
- Global role: champion free trade and human rights; 0.7% aid; Magnitsky sanctions; girls’ education; modern slavery/media freedom; support persecuted faith/LGBT conference; back major sporting bids.

Animal welfare
- Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end long live‑animal exports; extend ivory ban; ban primates as pets; measures on cat microchipping/theft.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and funding
- “Real change” to shift wealth and power from a privileged few, end austerity and tackle the climate emergency.
- Fair tax plan: raise income tax on earnings above £80,000; reverse parts of corporation tax cuts; no VAT rise; major anti-avoidance drive; 20:1 public-sector pay ratio cap; restore public sector pay with above-inflation rises.
- Investment: £400bn National Transformation Fund (incl. £250bn Green Transformation Fund); National Investment Bank and Regional Development Banks; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for schools, hospitals, housing and care.

Green Industrial Revolution
- Target majority of UK emissions cuts by 2030; 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low-carbon by 2030.
- 1 million climate jobs; ban fracking; windfall tax on oil firms; mass home retrofits and zero‑carbon standard for new homes; large-scale wind/solar, trial tidal and hydrogen; grid upgrades and storage.
- Public ownership of energy and water; community energy expansion.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership; electrification, HS2 to Scotland and “Crossrail for the North”; regulate/municipalise buses (free for under‑25s where councils run routes); boost walking/cycling; end new petrol/diesel car sales by 2030; expand EV charging.

Economy, work and rights
- Real Living Wage £10+ for all 16+; ban zero-hours; day‑one rights; single “worker” status; sectoral collective bargaining.
- Reduce average full-time week to 32 hours within a decade with no loss of pay; strengthen unions; inclusive ownership funds (up to 10% employee stakes).
- Tough late-payment rules; tailored support for self‑employed.

Public services, NHS and care
- End outsourcing and PFI; presumption to insource.
- NHS: average 4.3% annual funding rise; end privatisation; free prescriptions; restore public health; invest in staff, scanners, IT and mental health (parity with physical health).
- Social care: National Care Service with free personal care, better conditions for care workers, more packages to support independent living.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: restore Sure Start (Sure Start Plus), 30 hours free pre‑school for 2–4‑year‑olds, extend paid maternity leave to 12 months.
- Schools: fair funding, max primary classes of 30, scrap SATs, Arts Premium, bring academies/free schools under democratic local control, free school meals for all primaries.
- Further/higher: lifelong learning entitlements; abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; boost ESOL and adult learning.

Housing
- Build 1m+ council and social homes over a decade (150k/yr; 100k council); redefine “affordable” by income; end Right to Buy; “use it or lose it” on stalled sites.
- Private renting: rent controls, open‑ended tenancies, minimum standards/licensing, end no‑fault evictions; leasehold reform; £1bn fire safety fund; end rough sleeping in five years.

Justice, security and communities
- Rebuild neighbourhood policing; public health approach to crime; restore legal aid; reunify probation publicly; presumption against short sentences.
- Free full‑fibre broadband for all by 2030 via public ownership; Digital Rights and duty of care online.
- Strengthen local government, high streets (Post Bank, stop Crown Post Office closures), co-operatives and community wealth building.

Equality, migration and social security
- Department for Women and Equalities; close gender pay gap by 2030; stronger disability, race and LGBT+ rights.
- End the “hostile environment”; scrap 2014 Immigration Act; end indefinite detention; close Yarl’s Wood/Brook House; automatic right to remain for EU citizens.
- Scrap Universal Credit; immediate mitigations (end five‑week wait, end sanctions, scrap cap and two‑child limit); raise ESA; increase Carer’s Allowance; improve disability assessments.

Brexit and constitution
- Final‑say referendum within six months: credible leave deal (customs union, close single market alignment, rights and standards) vs remain; implement result.
- Abolish House of Lords for an elected Senate after a Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; curb dark money and lobbying.

Foreign policy and defence
- Human rights–led diplomacy; War Powers Act; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales linked to abuses; rebuild climate diplomacy.
- Maintain NATO and 2% defence spending; renew Trident; improve forces’ pay, housing and veteran support.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_F aligns more closely with this profile.
